materials.name: Inconel 625
materials.label: Corrosion resistance
materials.summary: Strong corrosion resistance in chloride-bearing and marine environments across a broad temperature range.
materials.headline: Inconel 625 Fasteners
materials.description: A nickel-chromium-molybdenum alloy considered for chloride exposure, seawater systems and corrosion-critical equipment where fabrication and dependable material traceability matter.
materials.forms: Bolts, studs, nuts, washers and round bar
materials.documentation: MTC / EN 10204 3.1 and testing as specified
materials.standards: ASTM B446, ASTM F468/F467 and project specifications
materials.service: Marine, offshore, chemical processing and pollution-control equipment

mechanical.tensileStrength: Typically 800-1,000 MPa, depending on product form and condition
mechanical.yieldStrength: Typically 340-630 MPa, depending on product form and condition
mechanical.elongation: Typically 30% or greater in annealed bar conditions
mechanical.condition: Solution annealed; cold-worked conditions are also available

comparison.temperatureCapability: Broad cryogenic-to-elevated-temperature capability; the governing fastener specification and service environment set the allowable limit.
comparison.corrosionCharacteristics: Strong resistance to seawater, chlorides and many industrial corrosive media, with useful oxidation resistance.
comparison.heatTreatment: Solution annealing when required by product form or specification
comparison.supplyCondition: Commonly annealed or solution treated; strength varies with cold work

materials.name: Inconel 718
materials.label: High strength
materials.summary: A precipitation-hardened nickel alloy for demanding loaded assemblies and elevated-temperature service.
materials.headline: Inconel 718 Fasteners
materials.description: A high-strength nickel-chromium alloy selected where mechanical performance, controlled heat treatment and verification of the final material condition are central to the order.
materials.forms: Bolts, studs, nuts, machined parts and round bar
materials.documentation: Heat treatment, mechanical testing and traceability
materials.standards: ASTM B637, AMS requirements and project specifications
materials.service: Power generation, aerospace-adjacent systems and high-load equipment

mechanical.tensileStrength: Typically 1,275 MPa or greater in common aged bar specifications
mechanical.yieldStrength: Typically 1,035 MPa or greater in common aged bar specifications
mechanical.elongation: Typically 12% or greater, depending on section and specification

comparison.temperatureCapability: Retains high mechanical strength in elevated-temperature service; commonly evaluated around applications up to approximately 700 C.
comparison.corrosionCharacteristics: Good general corrosion and oxidation resistance, selected primarily where high strength and thermal stability are required together.
comparison.heatTreatment: Solution treatment followed by controlled two-step age hardening
comparison.supplyCondition: Usually supplied solution treated and aged to the governing specification

materials.name: Hastelloy C-276
materials.label: Chemical service
materials.summary: A nickel-molybdenum-chromium alloy for severe chemical-processing and mixed-media environments.
materials.headline: Hastelloy C-276 Fasteners
materials.description: A corrosion-resistant alloy considered for aggressive acids, chlorides and process media where the material grade and manufacturing route must be reviewed together.
materials.forms: Bolts, studs, nuts, washers, machined parts and round bar
materials.documentation: PMI, material certification and inspection records
materials.standards: ASTM B574 and order-specific fastener requirements
materials.service: Chemical processing, waste treatment and pollution-control systems

mechanical.tensileStrength: Typically 690 MPa or greater in common solution-annealed product specifications
mechanical.yieldStrength: Typically 280 MPa or greater, depending on product form
mechanical.elongation: Typically 40% or greater in solution-annealed wrought forms

comparison.temperatureCapability: Temperature suitability depends strongly on the process medium; selection is driven by corrosion conditions before a general thermal limit is assigned.
comparison.corrosionCharacteristics: Exceptional resistance to a wide range of oxidizing and reducing acids, chlorides, pitting and crevice attack.
mediaAndConditions: Strong acids and mixed chemical media
comparison.heatTreatment: Solution annealing; avoid unqualified post-process thermal exposure
comparison.supplyCondition: Commonly supplied in the solution-annealed condition

materials.name: Monel K-500
materials.label: Marine strength
materials.summary: A precipitation-hardened nickel-copper alloy combining marine corrosion resistance with higher mechanical strength.
materials.headline: Monel K-500 Fasteners
materials.description: A nickel-copper alloy considered for loaded marine and offshore components where corrosion resistance, strength and control of the final heat-treated condition are reviewed together.
materials.forms: Bolts, studs, nuts, machined parts and round bar
materials.documentation: Material certification, heat treatment and mechanical testing
materials.standards: ASTM B865, applicable fastener standards and project specifications
materials.service: Marine hardware, pump components, offshore equipment and seawater systems

mechanical.tensileStrength: Typically 965-1,100 MPa for age-hardened bar, depending on size and condition
mechanical.yieldStrength: Typically 655-760 MPa for age-hardened bar, depending on size and condition
mechanical.elongation: Typically 20% or greater in many age-hardened bar conditions

comparison.temperatureCapability: Primarily selected for high-strength marine service; allowable elevated-temperature use must follow the applicable bolting code and heat-treated condition.
comparison.corrosionCharacteristics: Marine corrosion behavior broadly similar to Monel 400, combined with substantially higher age-hardened strength.
comparison.heatTreatment: Solution annealing followed by precipitation age hardening
comparison.supplyCondition: Hot-finished or cold-drawn and aged, as defined by size and specification
standardsSupport: ASME Code Case requirements where applicable

materials.name: A-286
materials.label: Thermal strength
materials.summary: A precipitation-hardened iron-nickel-chromium alloy for high-strength bolting and elevated-temperature assemblies.
materials.headline: A-286 Fasteners
materials.description: An age-hardenable alloy considered for fasteners requiring useful strength and oxidation resistance at elevated temperature, with heat treatment and mechanical properties defined by the governing specification.
materials.forms: Bolts, studs, nuts, screws, machined parts and round bar
materials.documentation: Heat treatment, mechanical testing and material traceability
materials.standards: ASTM A453 Grade 660, AMS requirements and project specifications
materials.service: Power generation, thermal equipment, aerospace-adjacent and industrial assemblies

mechanical.tensileStrength: Typically 965 MPa or greater in common precipitation-hardened bar conditions
mechanical.yieldStrength: Typically 655 MPa or greater in common precipitation-hardened bar conditions
mechanical.elongation: Typically 15% or greater, depending on specification and section

comparison.temperatureCapability: Designed for high-strength elevated-temperature service; final limits depend on fastener grade, stress level and heat-treatment route.
comparison.corrosionCharacteristics: Useful oxidation and general corrosion resistance, with selection normally driven by thermal strength rather than severe chemical resistance.
comparison.heatTreatment: Solution treatment followed by precipitation hardening to the specified grade
comparison.supplyCondition: Solution treated or fully precipitation hardened, depending on order requirements
